udf9e23e9e1: The cbp project and the Makefile (VSCode) project produce different build results
ub227d7e62f: The cbp project and the Makefile project use the same toolchain (compiler, linker, download tool, etc.) for building and linking. The difference is that the cbp project invokes the toolchain through Code::Blocks, while the Makefile project invokes it through make.
u5e6a7c408d: In other words, both ultimately use the same toolchain; only the user-facing interface differs.
u021e9466e6: If the settings of the two are equivalent, they should produce the same result.
u76c30d2272: The cbp project is not automatically kept in sync with the Makefile; the two are independent of each other. If you modify one, you must make the corresponding change in the other. For example, if you add a file to the cbp project, you must also add the same file to the Makefile; otherwise the two will produce different results.
ua3474d25f6: If you find that the two produce different results, consider the following possibilities:
u2f01c49437: The possibilities mentioned in the previous section
u24d3a31d00: The settings of the cbp project and the Makefile project differ. For example, you may have changed only the settings of the cbp project without making the corresponding change to the Makefile. If you modify the cbp project, you need to update the Makefile: either make the corresponding changes manually, or regenerate the Makefile by following ⟦1⟧How to Convert a Code::Blocks Project to a make/VSCode Project⟦/1⟧.
ub199c6b3de: Sometimes, after a build, the firmware file cannot be downloaded to the device. You can troubleshoot this with the following steps:
u8aa9035ac6: Wrong encoding of the download script download.bat
ua227655406: When Windows runs a ⟦1⟧bat⟦/1⟧ batch file, the file must be in the local encoding, which on Chinese systems is usually ⟦2⟧gbk⟦/2⟧. If ⟦3⟧download.bat⟦/3⟧ is encoded in ⟦4⟧utf-8⟦/4⟧, errors such as ⟦5⟧is not recognized as an internal or external command, operable program or batch file⟦/5⟧ (不是内部或外部命令，也不是可运行的程序) are reported, as shown below:
u3c2c2b79c7: In this case, consider changing the file encoding to ⟦2⟧gbk⟦/2⟧ with a tool such as ⟦1⟧Notepad++⟦/1⟧, or removing all Chinese characters from the file, which makes it equivalent to an ⟦3⟧ANSI⟦/3⟧-encoded file.
u739a9a70c1: Check the Code::Blocks build log for errors such as ⟦1⟧Device Offline⟦/1⟧, as shown below:
u16890a798d: If there are, the device is not connected to the computer or has not entered download mode. Possible causes include:
uee4eb8841a: The device is not plugged in correctly, the USB cable is loose, etc., so the device does not appear in Device Manager (see the explanation below)
u36cde2e8c4: The wrong device is plugged in, or the chip model does not match.
uf41c69cd84: When a device in download mode is connected correctly, an additional hidden disk should appear when you open My Computer (make sure your file browser is set to show hidden files and devices).
u35386466b7: In addition, under [My Computer] - [Device Manager] - [Disk drives], there should be a disk device whose name contains ⟦1⟧br**uboot1.0⟦/1⟧, ⟦2⟧bd**uboot1.0⟦/2⟧ or ⟦3⟧dv**uboot1.0⟦/3⟧.
u6d221ed11b: For more detailed steps, see ⟦1⟧Upgrading and Downloading⟦/1⟧
uff8085eb4d: If the corresponding device already appears in Device Manager but the ⟦1⟧Device Offline⟦/1⟧ message still appears, try the following methods in order:
u7dc4601ed8: Try downloading with administrator privileges, that is, open Code::Blocks as administrator, open the project, and then build and download. The download tool needs to access a physical device, which Windows may refuse in some cases, for example when you are logged in remotely.
u9cd257c63d: Check whether antivirus software, permission control software or similar software is installed on the computer, and whether the current user has permission to access USB devices (the download tool needs to read and write USB devices, and some computers may be configured to block access to USB devices for security and confidentiality reasons).
ud6d94e121a: If none of the above works, try another computer.
ua3f071dd12: Why can code sometimes be downloaded to the device only once?
u6d2ff5df47: A common mistake is that no programming pins were reserved when the board was designed. After the chip has been programmed once, the firmware starts running and the chip is no longer in programming mode. The most typical symptom is: ⟦1⟧a blank chip programs normally, but afterwards the chip can never enter download mode again⟦/1⟧. For details on how the board and its programming pins should be designed, contact your distributor or whoever provided the SDK.
u27be1ab326: KEY file does not match the chip
ub2c47d53bd: An error such as ⟦1⟧key mismatch⟦/1⟧ or ⟦2⟧mismatch⟦/2⟧ (不匹配) is reported. This error means that ⟦3⟧the key file does not match the chip⟦/3⟧. Check the parameters with which the download script ⟦4⟧download.bat⟦/4⟧ calls ⟦5⟧isd_download.exe⟦/5⟧:
u075c02dd7a: If the chip is a ⟦1⟧blank chip⟦/1⟧, there is ⟦2⟧no need⟦/2⟧ to specify the ⟦3⟧-key xxxxx⟦/3⟧ parameter when downloading; remove it. A blank chip does not need a key file.
u8bf831d87c: If the chip ⟦1⟧is not blank⟦/1⟧, you must specify the corresponding ⟦2⟧-key xxxxx⟦/2⟧ when downloading, where ⟦3⟧xxxxx⟦/3⟧ is the key file that matches the chip. ⟦4⟧Obtain this file from your distributor⟦/4⟧.
u6de02cac5b: Suppose you have confirmed that the chip is not blank and you specified a KEY file when downloading, but a mismatch error is still reported.
uae513db04e: This means that the KEY file you specified does not match the current chip. In other words, a different key file has already been programmed into this chip (not the KEY file you specified). Either you received a chip that was programmed incorrectly, or you received the wrong KEY file.
uaef8a9e940: Chips and KEY files must correspond one-to-one. Once a chip has been programmed with a KEY, its KEY cannot be changed, and the chip cannot be programmed with any other KEY file
uaf8952ca37: Note that the ⟦1⟧download.bat⟦/1⟧ script may call other bat scripts, so it is recommended to ⟦2⟧search the entire SDK project⟦/2⟧ for the keyword ⟦3⟧isd_download.exe⟦/3⟧.
uc32018e76a: If your KEY file name contains spaces, it is recommended to remove them, or to enclose the name in double quotes "", for example "key file with space.key".
u2ac784f3fa: To avoid problems, it is recommended that key file names contain no spaces at all.

udb7b259e7f: Some projects may contain several ⟦1⟧download.bat⟦/1⟧ download scripts. When you need to modify the download script, you first need to determine which one is the script to modify.
u034c8c8d86: The download script is a script that the SDK calls after building and linking are complete. It downloads the built and linked program to the device.
ub839a7373d: So the key question is how to find out which actions the SDK performs after building and linking are complete.
u100e0a0780: Finding the download script in a Code::Blocks project
u7202b94c8a: For Code::Blocks projects, the script executed after building and linking is called the ⟦1⟧post-build step⟦/1⟧, and this is where the download script is called.
u12636d051b: Finding the download script in a Makefile/VSCode project
u51c3774adc: For Makefile/VSCode projects, first find the corresponding Makefile.
uce876d969f: Under the ⟦1⟧all⟦/1⟧ target, there is a call named ⟦2⟧$(RUN_POST_SCRIPT)⟦/2⟧; this variable corresponds to the download script.
uf39825bcaa: In some SDKs, ⟦1⟧download.bat⟦/1⟧ is generated from ⟦2⟧download.c⟦/2⟧ and is regenerated on every build. If so, modify ⟦3⟧download.c⟦/3⟧ directly; otherwise your changes will be overwritten.
u4d7cdf09b8: In some SDKs, ⟦1⟧download.bat⟦/1⟧ also calls other ⟦2⟧download.bat⟦/2⟧ scripts; check the order in which they are called.
